title: What to Know About the AI-Triggered Cybersecurity Crisis
summary: PHP, a technology that underpins up to 70% of the world's websites, is under threat after a critical memory-handling flaw dubbed PHP2Shell was disclosed that could let attackers take control of affected systems. The US cybersecurity agency CISA urged companies to patch immediately or take vulnerable systems offline, and the tech industry is racing to deploy fixes.

title: Meta's Hunt for AI Capital Strikes a Raw Nerve on Wall Street
summary: Meta's search for new capital to fund its AI buildout unsettled investors, contributing to a sharp market reaction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 2.6%, while Treasury yields recorded their biggest drop since 2023.

title: Cyber Investors Don't Know What to Do With Their AI Worries
summary: AI is creating new security risks and lifting demand for protection, but it also exposes cybersecurity stocks to swings in sentiment around the technology. Shares of the five largest US cybersecurity companies all fell by double digits last week, far outpacing the broader selloff, before some began recovering losses.

title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion to New Mexico in Data Privacy Case
summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta Platforms to pay the state $25 billion, weeks after a jury found the company deceived users about its data-privacy practices, its efforts against hate speech and misinformation, and its handling of a third-party app tied to the 2018 Cambridge Analytica breach. Meta's chief legal officer said he is confident the company will prevail on appeal.

title: SpaceX Takes Conglomerate-Building to Sci-Fi Extremes
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that Elon Musk's mix of businesses under SpaceX will be a maze for investors to evaluate. The piece frames the company's expanding set of ventures as conglomerate-building taken to an extreme.

title: SB Energy Considers Waiting Until December or Later for an IPO
summary: SB Energy is weighing postponing its IPO to December or even next year, later than its earlier September target. The delay adds to signs of a stalled IPO market.

title: Datadog Offered to Buy Security Startup 'Upwind' For Nearly $4 Billion
summary: Datadog has offered close to $4 billion to acquire Upwind, a cloud security startup, according to The Information. The offer would be a major push by the observability vendor into cloud security.

title: Salesforce Wants a Fee Every Time an AI Agent Touches Its Software
summary: Starting around November, Salesforce plans to require customers to register external AI agents, such as Claude, as a step toward charging a fee for each action an agent takes in its apps. Atlassian, Workday, ServiceNow and Datadog are building similar tollgates as software vendors test whether agent fees can offset a possible decline in per-seat subscription revenue. Some consultants say customers may move data outside Salesforce to avoid the charges, and pricing has not yet been announced.

title: Utopai Becomes a Unicorn as Video AI Takes Off
summary: Utopai, a four-year-old AI film studio, has reached a valuation of $1 billion or more, and investors are reportedly already offering up to three times that. The deal highlights strong investor appetite for video AI.

title: Nokia and Nvidia Say AI-RAN Hype Is Justified as Nokia Touts Q3 AI Gains
summary: Nokia CEO Justin Hotard pointed to a boom in AI and cloud product sales in Q3 and said the vendor is well placed for growing infrastructure demand. Nokia and Nvidia executives told the MWL Podcast that close to 20 operators are lined up for lab and commercial AI-RAN trials.

title: AT&T CEO Stankey Argues Scale Matters in Satellite Direct-to-Device
summary: On the Q3 earnings call, AT&T CEO John Stankey outlined the advantages he sees over a potential SpaceX direct-to-device service. He cited AT&T's larger holdings of low-band spectrum, its scaled network and its ability to serve customers inside buildings.

title: Zuckerberg Claims Muse Agent Has Hit 10M Users
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on the Q3 earnings call that the company plans to expand its Muse personal agent and charge businesses for transactions it handles. He said the agent has reached 10 million users.

title: RBC's AI Chief Sounds the Alarm Over AI Agents
summary: Bruce Ross, RBC's AI chief, says the bank is concerned about letting AI agents access customer accounts and move money without the right safeguards in place.

title: The Signal Chats That Cost OpenAI Researchers Their Jobs
summary: OpenAI fired three safety researchers for mishandling sensitive information after security officers examined their phones and found some had enabled disappearing messages on Signal chats with an external AI-safety researcher. The researchers had reportedly been pushing to keep the workings of AI systems visible and to let outsiders examine them.

title: Meta's Muse Is Going Gangbusters. But Where Is the Payoff?
summary: Meta's Muse AI agent has reached 10 million downloads in a little over a month since launch. The piece asks how that adoption will translate into revenue at a time when investors are scrutinizing Meta's AI spending.

title: A Veteran of the Telecom Bust Navigates the AI Boom
summary: Ciena CEO Gary Smith, who lived through the telecom bust of the early 2000s, describes himself as suitably paranoid but optimistic about demand for optical networking gear driven by AI data-center build-outs. The profile frames how a survivor of the last infrastructure cycle is managing the current one.

title: The Best Boards in America Are Helping Drive AI Strategy
summary: The WSJ Leadership Institute's Best Boards 2026 ranking of S&P 500 companies shows top boards, including those at Lam Research, eBay, Trimble, Lumentum and Nasdaq, playing an active role in AI strategy. Common traits include directors with technology expertise, dedicated technology committees and dashboards that track AI metrics such as agents deployed and AI-generated revenue.

title: SK Hynix Scraps U.S. IPO of Flash-Memory Unit Solidigm
summary: SK Hynix shelved plans for a U.S. public offering of Solidigm, which had aimed to raise roughly $10 billion to $15 billion, citing market conditions and share-price trends. It is the latest listing pulled amid fears of an AI bubble, following Australian data-center operator Firmus Grid's cancelled IPO earlier this month.

title: AI Rout Hits Tech Stocks as Nasdaq Posts Worst Day Since June
summary: The Nasdaq composite fell 2.6% on Thursday, its worst day since June, with Meta down 7% and the PHLX semiconductor index off 6.7% as data-center-linked stocks from Alphabet to Amazon also dropped. Premarket trading on Friday suggested the selloff might find a floor for now.

title: Cyber Chiefs Face Stark Options to Fix Global PHP Security Flaw
summary: A flaw dubbed PHP2Shell lets attackers steal data from web servers and launch attacks on site visitors, leaving companies to either bolster defenses and race hackers or take sites offline. Amazon researchers saw exploitation four days before public disclosure, and there is no easy fix, with remediation and recovery costs mounting.

title: Chinese Hackers Spied on Thousands of Companies After Breaching ConnectWise
summary: Hackers linked to China's government spied on about 2,250 companies after stealing credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service, according to Microsoft researchers. ConnectWise shut the service down to investigate and expects to restore it by the end of the weekend, while Microsoft said AI agents helped the attackers attempt nearly 3,000 sign-ins a minute.

title: Lasers, Robots and AI: The Fight to Save Salmon Goes High-Tech
summary: Salmon producers such as Mowi are deploying AI cameras, net-cleaning robots and blue-light lasers that zap sea lice to cut losses in ocean pens. About 14% of farmed Atlantic salmon in Norway died before maturity last year, and demand from health trends, sushi and weight-loss drugs is pushing the industry toward technology to improve survival.

title: Instacart Is Exploring a Sale
summary: The Information reports that Instacart has been in talks to sell itself, a move that could end a 14-year run as an independent company.

title: VC Firms Tap LP Pools, Warehouse Loans for Speedy AI Cash
summary: Venture capital firms are using new financing methods, from warehouse loans to inviting limited partners to co-invest, to keep pace with the ballooning size of AI startup funding rounds.

title: Ramp Investors Went Nuclear Against Airwallex After Doomed Deal
summary: Investors in fintech Ramp reacted aggressively against rival Airwallex after a deal between the two companies collapsed, according to The Information. The article details the fallout from the failed transaction between the payments and spend-management startups.

title: SpaceX Eyes 80,000 US Cell Sites for Starlink Mobile
summary: SpaceX is reportedly in talks with tower companies to secure access to at least 80,000 US sites as it advances plans for a nationwide mobile network to rival AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile US.

title: CCS Insight Predicts SpaceX Buys an Operator and Apple Leads 6G Devices
summary: Analyst firm FDM CCS Insight published bold predictions for 2027 and beyond, including that SpaceX acquires a mobile operator and Apple leads 6G device launches.

title: UAE-Led Operation Identifies $39 Billion Linked to AI-Enabled Fraud
summary: A UAE-led international operation targeting AI-enabled fraud and cross-border scam networks identified more than $39 billion in funds and cryptocurrencies linked to scam activity.
